text: A diffractive deep neural network (D2NN) built from passive metasurface layers has a fundamental limit on its expressive power. What is it?
choices: It cannot be trained by backpropagation
It can classify only audio, never images
Passive diffraction is linear, so a stack of layers collapses to a single linear operation unless nonlinearity is added
Each diffractive layer must be thicker than 1 mm
explanation: Because passive diffraction is a linear operation, cascading layers yields only another linear map, so without optical nonlinearity a D2NN cannot match a deep nonlinear network. D2NNs are in fact trained by backpropagation through a differentiable diffraction (angular-spectrum) model and reach 91-93% on MNIST images, so the other options are false.
